title: Jazz players recording with strings
summary: John Wilson calls strings a death wish.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I don't know why jazz players, they'll go with a company and they get -- their records will start to sell, so I
guess it's a big reward for the company. Or as John Wilson called it, he said, it seems to be the death wish of jazz musicians to record with strings. And I think that's the best way of putting it.
Why jazz musicians want to record with strings I'll never know, because I think it stinks.
I think Pearl Bailey put it aptly. She said, that seems to make them kick them out of the motel type and put them into the hotel type.
Oh, is that what it is?

Well, maybe. Well, John Wilson said it's just a death wish they have. They don't turn out too good. But of course Charlie Parker would sound good with people banging on tincans behind him. And some of those rhythm sections he had sounded like that. I listened to some of those earlier records and I can't believe what I hear. Some of those rhythm sections weren't too good.
